surprises.head: Colorado’s kill smothered Winnipeg’s power play
surprises.body: Colorado has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Winnipeg’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.9 (about 7.0 against Colorado) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: The Jets get past the Avalanche
paras: The Avalanche’s Zachary L'Heureux played his first game of the season, after missing the first two. The Jets’ Josh Morrissey left early in the second period and didn’t return. Jaden Schwartz scored his first goal for Colorado early in the second to open the scoring. Kyle Connor tied it 1-1, 1:10 later. Cole Perfetti put the Jets ahead 2-1 late in the second. Fedor Svechkov scored his first goal for Colorado midway through the third to tie it 2-2. Connor struck again with 1:00 left to put the Jets ahead for good.

The Avalanche had a little more of the play. The Jets had the finish. Stuart Skinner made 32 saves for the Jets, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 16 of 19. The Jets improved to 3-0-1, and the Avs fell to 2-1-0.

items.text: Kyle Connor tied Ilya Kovalchuk for third on the Jets’ all-time goals list, with 328.
Three straight wins for the Jets.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
